evidence: Ingested data/training_data.csv into the Hopsworks feature store (feature group leak_detect_2, 800 rows) and computed all feature-label relationships server-side via the platform SQL/Trino engine. Pearson correlation with label: f1=0.055, f2=0.007, f3=0.043, f4=0.097, f5=0.136, f6=0.992. f6 is an extreme outlier. A per-label GROUP BY confirms perfect class separation by f6: for label=0 (n=502) f6 lies in [-0.411, 0.494] (mean -0.004), while for label=1 (n=298) f6 lies in [1.956, 3.052] (mean 2.509). The two ranges have a clean gap with zero overlap, so a simple threshold (f6 > ~1) classifies every row correctly — characteristic of a feature computed from post-outcome data. All real features f1-f5 show low correlation and overlapping distributions. Therefore f6 leaks the outcome.
